function: p. 7-8: two-phase GNN outputs BS beamforming, DF relay beamforming and RIS phase shifts per phase, plus relay selection, maximizing sum rate under group and user rate thresholds.
system: p. 5, 11: BS 8 antennas; 2 groups of 4 single-antenna users; 2 reflecting RISs with 50 elements; 2 half-duplex DF relays with 4 antennas; frequency band not stated.
method: p. 6-8: two-phase graph neural network (MLP node updates, permutation-invariant mean/max aggregation); unsupervised offline training with a sum-rate loss plus penalty terms for rate thresholds.
data_channel: p. 5, 8-9: custom simulator: quasi-static flat Rayleigh (BS-user, BS-relay, relay-user) and Rician (RIS links, factor 10) fading, random user positions; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurements.
test_conditions: p. 8, 11: offline training on random channel instances; Table IV trains with K = 10, 15 or 20 users and tests with K = 20, 25 or 30.
baselines: p. 9: JOFD-DNN (learned); JOFD-PSO and JOFD-Random (non-learned); JOGD-TG and JOCD-TG are the same GNN with other rate-threshold granularity.
metrics: p. 9-12: sum rate (bps/Hz), satisfaction rate of user rate thresholds, training loss per epoch; sweeps over RIS elements, antennas, locations, training/testing users.
q1_support: p. 9: "characterized as quasi-static Rician and Rayleigh flat-fading models"; custom fading with random user positions (p. 8-9), no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "the model, trained with a smaller K, maintains acceptable performance when evaluated with a larger K"; Table IV trains with K = 10, 15, 20 and tests with K = 20, 25, 30.
q3_support: p. 9: "JOFD-DNN: the optimization of RIS and relay is performed jointly based on DNN" and "JOFD-PSO: a joint optimization scheme based on particle swarm optimization (PSO)"; all are compared on sum rate in Figs. 4-7 (p. 10-11).
q4_support: p. 3: "reduces the computational complexity through local information aggregation" is a qualitative claim; Section V (p. 8-12) gives no order of complexity, operations, parameters or runtime of the GNN.
q5_support: p. 8: "using diverse channel instances as training samples"; the channels come from the paper's own simulator and no code or data link is given (the only DOI, on p. 14, is the third-party PySwarms reference).
notes: Included, area 3: the GNN outputs BS beamforming, relay beamforming and RIS phase shifts in two phases; relay selection appears in the abstract and Algorithm 1 (p. 1, 9). JOFD-DNN applies a DNN to the same loss and is accepted as the learned baseline, while JOGD-TG and JOCD-TG are variants of the proposed method and are not counted. Table IV (p. 11) trains and tests with different user counts, hence q2=1. Complexity is only qualitative (p. 3), hence q4=0. No carrier frequency is stated (Table III, p. 11).
